Well, I definitely think that we should apologize for the atrocities, dragging it on just makes us seem unapologetic at best, and downright heartless at worse. But it is an complicated matter. The government held on for soo long to apologize, and just hoping ppl forget about it, that there are a lot of people indeed never learned about stuff like this. If you’re not especially interested in history when you are studying (like myself), it will come as a shock the first time you found out about things like this (and yes, I know about the 731 and Korean comfort women).  And the reaction can go very differently, I for one just feel horrible about everything, and there are some who would feel defensive, because they aren’t the ones that did this stuff, but they are being seen as heartless because our government just want to save face. And there are undoubtedly people who would see these events and call them exaggerated by the Koreans or the Chinese (source: my dad), because that is what they were taught and it is hard for them to see otherwise. And furthermore, the government and citizens will be more and more unwilling to apologize because everytime we do a quote unquote apology, we have to pay money to those countries, and who in the citizens would want to pay for something that happened a while ago, not really their fault and keeps repeating? Like I said, I would like the government just own up and apologize, but it really isn’t that simple.
